original_value: Synthesizing face sketches with both common and specific information from photos has been recently attracting considerable attentions in digital entertainment. However, the existing approaches either make the strict similarity assumption on face sketches and photos, leading to lose some identity-specific information, or learn the direct mapping relationship from face photos to sketches by the simple neural network, resulting in the lack of some common information. In this paper, we propose a novel face sketch synthesis based on the Markov random neural fields including two structures. In the first structure, we utilize the neural network to learn the non-linear photo-sketch relationship and obtain the identity-specific information of the test photo, such as glasses, hairpins and hairstyles. In the second structure, we choose the nearest neighbors of the test photo patch and the sketch pixel synthesized in the first structure from the training data which ensure the common information of Miss or Mr Average. Experimental results on the Chinese University of Hong Kong face sketch database illustrate that our proposed framework can preserve the common structure and capture the characteristic features. Compared with the state-of-the-art methods, our method achieves better results in terms of both quantitative and qualitative experimental evaluations.

result.paraphrase: Synthesizing face sketches from photos while preserving both common and specific information has recently attracted considerable attention in digital entertainment. Existing methods either impose a strict similarity assumption between face sketches and photos, which causes some identity-specific details to be lost, or use a simple neural network to learn a direct photo-to-sketch mapping, which can miss some common information. In this paper, we present a new face sketch synthesis method based on Markov random neural fields with two structures. The first structure uses a neural network to learn the nonlinear photo-sketch relationship and extract identity-specific information from the test photo, such as glasses, hairpins, and hairstyles. The second structure selects the nearest neighbors of the test photo patch and the sketch pixel synthesized in the first structure from the training data, thereby preserving the common information of Miss or Mr Average. Experimental results on the Chinese University of Hong Kong face sketch database show that our framework can maintain the common structure and capture characteristic features. Compared with state-of-the-art methods, our approach achieves better quantitative and qualitative evaluation results.
